proposed_fixes.title: Report editor-hotkey registration failures accurately
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Settings capture can succeed while native RegisterHotKey fails for an OS-owned/conflicting chord; the current registration path only logs failure.

prerequisites: Use a disposable configuration and record Windows build; establish an unused working editor chord first.
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable and current development build
steps: Capture and save a reported chord and verify the persisted modifier/key values.
Record RegisterHotKey success or its exact error after Settings applies the change, then activate outside the shortcut input.
Compare an unused chord and the Windows Search/Magnifier-associated cases with PowerToys elevated and unelevated.
Restore the working chord and verify failed registration does not leave misleading Settings state or silently lose editor access.
reproduce.expected_result: Supported chords persist and activate; conflicts are distinguished from capture errors and explained without claiming ownership of every Windows chord.

inferences: An OS-owned or already-registered chord can fail after Settings accepts its text; a control capture problem is also possible and must be separated by saved-key and registration observations.
issue_context.analysis: The report needs a focused maintainer comparison of captured value, saved value, registration result and actual activation. A useful fix follows the demonstrated boundary and must not silently steal Windows shortcuts or discard a working binding.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report, nine replies and timeline, including the maintainer distinction between shortcut control and Windows ownership.
Inspected current editor-hotkey observer and RegisterHotKey failure logging; did not assume the old low-level-hook proposal was implemented or appropriate.
known_information: The original0.20.1 report and nine replies identify Win+Q, Win+Z and Win+Esc editor shortcuts; participants observe Windows Search and a maintainer notes the Magnifier binding.
Current FancyZones::UpdateHotkey unregisters the previous binding, calls RegisterHotKey and logs its failure; setting-change observation invokes this registration path.
The current source therefore has a concrete registration-failure boundary; it does not prove which historical shortcut failed registration or that all reported chords are unconditionally reservable.
